<reason>CON won by holding the motion’s comparison: special duty-of-care versus ordinary entertainment plus ordinary consumer rules. After PRO conceded opted-in jealousy with a working disable and ordinary subscription endings, CON showed the leftover wrongs (ignored controls, payment-conditioned persona panic) are identifiable coercion or abusive collection, not a reason to regulate attachment itself. PRO’s product-difference story stayed vivid but was narrowed until it no longer justified treating companionship as a distinct legal relationship.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2 used PRO’s A1/A2 answers as a concession collapse: if requested, disableable, retention-optimized romance and post-bonding cutoff are allowed, remaining harms reduce to commercial pressure that entertainment-status consumer rules can already target.</best_rebuttal>
